facts.condition: Any such improvement must also satisfy the aggregate obstruction obtained by combining the two assignments in which the auxiliaries occupy different coordinates; this remains only a necessary condition.

A finite two-use Marton candidate cannot improve on the doubled single-use benchmark unless the decomposition residual is above zero for each of the four ways of assigning the two auxiliaries to the two coordinates; failure for any assignment excludes that candidate.

assumptions: Satisfying these obstructions is not assumed to establish an improvement, additivity, a support bound, or the exact sum-capacity.
The canonical half-skew channel uses the established single-use Marton benchmark normalization.
The previously accepted tuple-law decomposition applies to arbitrary finite two-use Marton auxiliaries without presuming coordinatewise product structure.
